operators.label: Reversal
operators.intent: Turn the situation of the passage so that something moves to its opposite: fortune, knowledge, power, allegiance or expectation.
guidance: Set up the prior state clearly enough that the turn registers.
Make the reversal feel inevitable in hindsight: plant its cause earlier in the passage.
Place the turn at a precise moment and let the passage register its consequences.
avoid: Explaining the reversal after it lands

variants.label: Of Fortune
variants.intent: Success becomes failure, or failure becomes success.
guidance: Let the character's own action trigger the turn.
Show the new situation concretely.

variants.label: Of Knowledge (Recognition)
variants.intent: A discovery transforms the meaning of what came before.
guidance: Plant the detail that will be reinterpreted.
Stage the moment of recognition in the character's perception.
Let earlier lines read differently afterwards.

variants.label: Of Power
variants.intent: The dominant and subordinate positions in the scene swap.
guidance: Establish who holds power at the start.
Make the shift hinge on a specific leverage: information, resource, witness.
Show both characters registering the change.

variants.label: Of Allegiance
variants.intent: An ally becomes an opponent, or the reverse.
guidance: Seed motive earlier.
Reveal through action rather than announcement.
Keep the character's logic coherent.

variants.label: Of Expectation
variants.intent: The reader's or character's assumption about what is happening proves wrong.
guidance: Lead expectation with fair cues.
Turn it with a single decisive detail.
Avoid cheating: the true reading must fit all the facts.

variants.label: Moral Reversal
variants.intent: Sympathy shifts: the wronged party is revealed as wrongdoer, or the reverse.
guidance: Keep both readings plausible until the turn.
Reveal through a specific act or fact.
Let the protagonist's judgment be implicated.

operators.label: Clue
operators.intent: Embed a piece of information that will matter later, visible enough to be fair but not so visible that it is obvious.
guidance: Make the clue a concrete, checkable detail.
Give it a plausible surface reason to be in the passage.
Do not draw the character's or narrator's attention to its significance unless the variant calls for it.
avoid: Adding more than one new clue unless asked

variants.label: Fair-Play
variants.intent: A clue an attentive reader could use to solve the puzzle.
guidance: State the detail plainly once.
Surround it with ordinary details of similar weight.

variants.label: Buried in a List
variants.intent: Hide the clue among other items of description or procedure.
guidance: Place it in the middle of a list, not first or last.
Match its phrasing to its neighbors.

variants.label: Red Herring
variants.intent: A misleading clue that points plausibly in the wrong direction.
guidance: Make it more noticeable than true clues.
Keep it honest: it must have an innocent explanation consistent with the facts.

variants.label: Absence
variants.intent: The clue is something missing that should be present.
guidance: Establish the expected pattern.
Let the absence pass quickly, noted but not examined.

variants.label: Dialogue Slip
variants.intent: A character reveals more than they should in speech.
guidance: Make the slip small and natural.
Let the scene move on before anyone reacts.

variants.label: Expert Observation
variants.intent: The clue is registered through the character's specialist knowledge.
guidance: Use accurate professional terminology sparingly.
Let the character note the detail without yet grasping its full significance.
